transcript.text: Good morning Rushil Bhatia. Here is your daily news for Sunday, August 9. In today's briefing: top headlines, bhopal and madhya pradesh, business and markets, money, tax and personal finance, science and technology, development and policy, across india, around the world. Let's begin.

transcript.title: Top headlines
transcript.text: First, the stories leading the news this morning. IAF wing commander 'honey-trapped' by Pak operatives; charged for alleged info leak. A Wing Commander in the Indian Air Force is currently under serious accusations of leaking critical defense information. It is reported that he fell victim to a honey trap orchestrated by operatives from Pakistani intelligence using social media. Allegations suggest he secretly installed software designed to steal data on a colleague's device. Prior to his arrest by the Delhi Police, he was under close scrutiny by the IAF. Vance calls PM after US Senate passes 100 percent tariff bill, discusses boosting ties. On Saturday, VP JD Vance engaged in a conversation with PM Narendra Modi, reiterating both nations' dedication to strengthen partnerships in vital sectors such as trade, defense, and upcoming technologies. They shared insights on international matters of shared concern, coinciding with the US Senate's approval of a bill focused on Russian oil transactions. US rejects China's attempt to enforce new restrictions at Scarborough Reef. The United States has firmly rejected China's maneuvers at Scarborough Reef, asserting that Beijing's environmental assertions are hindering Filipino fishermen from accessing their traditional fishing grounds. As a staunch ally in the Indo-Pacific, Washington stands in solidarity with the Philippines, highlighting China's contentious approach of using legal claims to assert maritime rights. This reaffirmation underscores US commitment to its allied nation's interests amidst complex maritime disputes. Australia pacer takes 8/25 as Bangladesh bowled out for 54, lose match by innings. Campbell Thompson was the main contributor to Bangladesh's collapse, taking eight wickets for 25 runs in the second innings at Marrara Oval. The 22-year-old left-arm fast bowler had taken two wickets late on Friday before returning on Saturday morning to claim six more as Bangladesh lost eight wickets for 35 runs. Captain of turbulence-hit Phuket-Delhi flight may have failed dope test. During a turbulent flight from Phuket to Delhi, the captain of an Air India aircraft reportedly tested positive for psychoactive substances. The turbulence caused a significant scare, resulting in hospitalization for thirteen passengers and four crew members. The Directorate General of Civil Aviation is conducting a detailed investigation, and the flight crew has been suspended from flying duties as per standard procedures. Elon Musk says Starship Flight 13 recovery 'not looking good' after splashdown. SpaceX's Starship recovery is struggling against the tumultuous waters of the Indian Ocean, with Elon Musk admitting the situation appears grim. Despite these difficulties, engineers managed to capture invaluable images of essential spacecraft components. This visual data is expected to contribute significantly to enhancements in Starship design and its reusability. Notably, the mission marked SpaceX's most successful Starship test flight to date. Government appoints 30 judges to high courts of Calcutta, MP, Karnataka, Madras. The law ministry notified thirty new judges for four high courts on Saturday. Madras High Court received fifteen appointments, while Calcutta got eight and Karnataka six. Judicial officers and advocates were elevated to the benches, with most appointed as additional judges. Over sixty lakh cases are pending across India's twenty-five high courts. Agni-4 fills key gaps in India's missile arsenal, strengthens China deterrence. India successfully tested its Agni-4 medium-range ballistic missile last Thursday. This missile bridges a critical gap in India's strategic deterrence capabilities. The Agni-4 missile can carry nuclear and conventional payloads with a 4,000 km range. It features an advanced heat shield and a precise guidance system for accuracy. Proposed MDR for UPI transactions will be nominal, says government. The government has pledged that the upcoming UPI merchant discount rate will be minimal. This fee will be applicable only to certain merchants and transactions that surpass a designated threshold. Importantly, person-to-person UPI payments will remain free for all users. This initiative is designed to enhance the sustainability of India's digital payment ecosystem and facilitate service expansion into rural and semi-urban regions. Michael Dell's son's startup offers $695 alternative to costly home generators. Zach Dell's Base Power is installing home battery systems across America. These systems offer backup power and reduce electricity bills for customers. The company aims to replace expensive gas generators with its innovative technology. Base Power is rapidly expanding its operations and customer base nationwide. 6 years after NDA exit, Punjab's SAD backs delimitation push. Akali Dal president Sukhbir Singh Badal now supports the women's reservation law rollout. This move signals the government's potential revival of the Constitution amendment bill. The government is also seeking support from DMK and NCP(SP) for the measure. The bill aims to increase Lok Sabha's strength by fifty percent. Houston man's solo trash cleanups grow into 100-volunteer movement. A Houston resident's initiative to clean up neglected areas has blossomed into a vibrant volunteer movement. With one hundred dedicated individuals now on board, their mission is to remove illegally dumped waste. Collaborating with local organizations and harnessing the power of social media, city officials and law enforcement are boosting efforts to tackle this pressing issue, ultimately enhancing the community's aesthetics and the well-being of its residents.
